OPEN LEMMA of block 33 (PR #8177; setting in blocks 25, 30, 32: PRs #8168, #8174, #8176). Two-level noisy majority automaton in level time on Z^3: a site's three predecessors are z - e_1, z - e_2, z - e_3; seeds S (no 1-predecessor), amplified sites A (exactly one), processed sites (two or more). Counted family of marked explanation trees; rooted value v(z) := min over trees of the family containing z with all nodes at levels <= level(z) of E - 3(|S| - 1) - |A|; a site is TIGHT when v = 0. THE LEMMA: a processed site all of whose 1-predecessors are tight processed sites has a rooted tree of cost at most zero. It is equivalent to the unit budget c* = 1 and would lower the proved ordering threshold on the line (p,1,2) from 4165 to 453. Evidence: no violation in about 10^4 hill-climbed realizations; structural searches found no tight sibling pairs at all. title: Do massive records bound by a static possibility shift carry their binding energy as inertia?
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 2: Do massive records bound by a static possibility shift carry their binding energy as inertia?. LANDED FIRST: origin/main is the science authority; read each named note as landed (git show origin/main:docs/<note>) before any PR branch, and where a PR's wording differs from the landed text, the landed text controls. Blocks 115, 133, 139 and 142 are OPEN hand-off PRs (#9157, #9191, #9201, #9227): read them on their branches (gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName; git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). Block 115 is a harvest of Grok-refereed attempts; blocks 139 and 142 are the supervisor's own derivations (Claude), NOT refereed by another family; nothing in them is adopted. SETTING: block 139 (PR #9201): the staggered mass m eps (eps = (-1)^{x1+x2+x3}) is the only site rest energy that keeps the books; a free massive walker has E^2 = sum sin^2 k + m^2, so at rest c^2 = d^2(E^2/2)/dk^2 = 1 along each axis (its inertia equals its rest energy). Block 133 (PR #9191): a massive body at rest sits on one sublattice, so two massive records at rest are never neighbours: a nearest-neighbour term binds them only through the other sublattice, and a two-step term (separation 2) binds them directly. Block 142 (PR #9227): compact pairs of massless records bound as neighbours are much heavier or lighter than their energy (c^2 = 1/2 on the line; no weight one along all axes in space). A supervisor exploration (floating point, NOT a result; the line, walkers sigma_z D + m eps, m = 4, one record per site, attraction V at separation 2, the pair's total momentum sector of the two-site translation) found the pair's weight W = E0 d^2E/dK^2 at rest to be 0.117, 0.201, 0.411 and 0.539 for V = -0.5, -0.3, -0.15 and -0.115; these fit W = 1/(4m|V|), which is block 142's half-line law for the pair on the massive records' own sublattice (relative hopping cos(K/2)/(4m)): W = 1 at the binding threshold |V| = 1/(4m), and near it 1 - W is of order (lattice spacing)/(pair size), a lattice effect of the pair's size. For two free relativistic bodies bound by a static potential U, expanding sqrt(m^2 + p^2) gives W = 1 + <U>/(2m) - <T>/m + ... (T the internal kinetic energy): a static binding's energy does not carry its share of inertia, and W falls short of one by about the binding fraction, however large the pair. The binding-fraction part is separate from the size part and does not shrink with the pair's size. TASK: (a) on the line and on Z^3, for two massive records under one record per site bound by a weak static two-step (or neighbour) term, compute the pair's weight exactly or with rigorous bounds as the pair loosens toward the binding threshold, and decide whether W - 1 approaches -(<T> - <U>/2)/m (the static formula) or 0; (b) separate the lattice part (the pair's size in lattice units) from the binding-fraction part; (c) decide whether any form of the binding term that depends on the pair's motion (for example on the records' two-step momenta or currents, or a term carried by the clock or the member) makes W = 1 at leading order in the binding fraction. HIT: (a) exact or rigorously bounded, or (c) settled. REGIME NOTE (added with refill p): on the lattice the pair's weight has a size part of order k^2 (k the constituents' wave number in lattice units) and a binding-fraction part of order T/m ~ k^2/m^2; the binding-fraction part dominates only when m << 1 in lattice units, the regime of masses far below the lattice scale, so study (a) and (b) there (the exploration at m = 4 measured the size part). LANDED FIRST: origin/main is the science authority; read each named note as landed (git show origin/main:docs/<note>) before any PR branch, and where a PR's wording differs from the landed text, the landed text controls. Blocks 137, 140 and 143 are OPEN hand-off PRs (#9197, #9203, #9229): read them on their branches (gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName; git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). They are the supervisor's own derivations (Claude), NOT refereed by another family; nothing in them is adopted. SETTING: block 143 (PR #9229) shows, for two records of block 54's walk, that a kept total energy current makes the pair transparent (T3), and that a transparent finite-rank change of the free pair has perturbation determinant identically one (T5), so nothing local keeps the books under one record per site. T5 rests on one named assumption (A'): at some total wave vector K0 the four band functions E(q) = s1 eps(K0/2 + q) + s2 eps(K0/2 - q) (eps = (sum_a sin^2 k_a)^(1/2), s1, s2 = +-1) have only nondegenerate stationary points on the torus, away from the cone points where eps vanishes; by persistence of nondegenerate stationary points this then holds near K0, which suffices. Also check the cone points (eps = 0), where the band functions are not smooth, for stationary behaviour. HIT: (A') certified at one K0 in the plane (and in space), with exact checks. HIT: (a) and (b) exact at the stated order, with exact checks. SETTING: block 54's walk h(k) = sum_a sigma_a sin k_a; one record per site (block 78); block 152 (landed) T2: for antisymmetric pairs the hard core's T-matrix is |c><c|/G_cc(z), c the coincident singlet, G_cc = <c|(h0 - z)^-1|c>, and the rate of change of the two-step momentum is 2 pi |<c|q>|^2 rho_c (gbar - g(q))/|G_cc(E + i0)|^2; the owner's review of block 152 did not exclude threshold poles. The supervisor's observation (unchecked): the staggered sign (-1)^(x1+x2+x3) on both records anticommutes with the two-record generator, fixes c and commutes with the exclusion, so G_cc(-z) = -G_cc(z) in every fiber; hence Re G_cc(E + i0) is odd and Im G_cc even in E, and at K = 0 the contact amplitude has a pole at E = 0. Find the small-E, small-K behaviour of G_cc(E + i0; K) in the regime E ~ |K| where upper-band pairs collide: the (+, +) density, the (+, -) contributions, and the real part. Hence give the rate at which collisions change g for slow records, as powers of E and K. (3) Say what this does to block 152's rate formula near threshold, as landed (the owner's review did not exclude threshold poles). The supervisor's prior: the threshold enhancement survives at E ~ |K| and the rate per pair falls as E^3 rather than E^5 (0.4). HIT: exact statements for any of (1)-(3).
